title: XL Airways Germany 888T

agencies.name: Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety

summary: XL Airways Flight 888T was an acceptance test flight of an Airbus A320 on 27 November 2008. Incorrect maintenance procedures allowed water to enter and freeze in the angle-of-attack sensors, rendering them inoperative. During descent, the crew attempted to perform a slow-flight test at approximately 8,000 to 6,000 feet, below the intended test altitude. The aircraft crashed into the Mediterranean Sea 7 km off the French coast, killing all seven people on board.
probable_cause: The probable cause was incorrect maintenance procedures that allowed water to enter and freeze in the angle-of-attack sensors, combined with the crew's decision to perform a test maneuver at dangerously low altitude during the descent phase.

factors.evidence: incorrect maintenance procedures allowed water to enter and freeze in the angle-of-attack sensors during flight, rendering them inoperative
angle-of-attack sensors provided erroneous data due to ice blockage rendering them inoperative
crew attempted to perform slow flight check at approximately 8,000 to 6,000 feet, when procedure was supposed to be performed at approximately 14,000 feet
aircraft crashed into the Mediterranean Sea 7 km off Canet-en-Roussillon with all seven on board killed while attempting test maneuver at dangerously low altitude with inoperative sensors

events.text: Flight took off from Perpignan Airport on acceptance flight test
Crew requested clearance to test at 39,000 feet for auxiliary power unit testing
Captain Horrell described actions required for slow flight check as aircraft descended through approximately 8,000 to 6,000 feet
Aircraft passing through cloud layers during descent with erroneous angle-of-attack sensor inputs from frozen sensors rendering them inoperative
Aircraft crashed into Mediterranean Sea 7 km off French coast Canet-en-Roussillon killing all seven people on board

notes: BEA full report with complete findings and recommendations

recommendations.text: Detail in EU-OPS the various types of non-revenue flights that an operator from a EU state is authorised to perform

Require that non-revenue flights be described precisely in the approved parts of the operations manual, including their preparation, programme and operational framework as well as the qualifications and training of crews
Require that such flights be subject to an authorisation, or a declaration by the operator, on a case-by-case basis
Ensure that equipment installation conditions during tests performed by equipment manufacturers are representative of those on the aeroplane
Undertake a safety study with a view to improving certification standards of warning systems for crews during reconfigurations of flight control systems
In cooperation with manufacturers, improve training exercises and techniques relating to approach-to-stall recovery
